name: markdown-anchoring
body:
Markdown is now a scanned language (`requirements.requirement.markdown-frontend`): .md/.markdown files enter the graph as File nodes (FQN = the absolute path) with Struct section nodes, so `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` and the root AGENTS.md become File/Struct nodes — the very `.md` paths this note previously called unscannable. That does NOT move the agent-prompt component's coverage anchor: the distributed agent prompts are embedded constants in the binary (`include_str!` in src/main.rs) delivered to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite`, so the durable delivered artifact is the embedded text plus its install path, and the component's `implemented-by` stays on the embedding/install Rust (`apg.main`, `apg.install_suite`) — never on a `.md` path. No exclusion of the template tree is required: the anchor is chosen for delivery semantics, not as a workaround for non-scannability.

Drift semantics (UNCHANGED): an `implemented-by` target is Real when its FQN is in the scanned code-FQN universe (src/main.rs:1342-1364 — Module/Struct/Function/File records with no `status` set), Pending when the plan declares it planned, and Drift otherwise — a write-time error (src/layers.rs:1295-1329). Once the markdown frontend lands and `.md` files are scanned, a `.md` File FQN enters that universe and is therefore a LEGITIMATE `implemented-by` target; before it lands (and for any `.md` path the scan does not accept), a `.md` target is still Drift. So this component avoiding a `.md` anchor is a deliberate choice — the embedded constant is the delivered artifact — not a claim that every `.md` target is drift. The drift rule keys off the code universe, and scanned `.md` File nodes are part of it.
